checks.detail: the Fourier-plane spacing f_tube*lambda/(n*shape[0]*pitch) = 6.4103 um is within 1.38% of the 6.5 um camera pitch but not equal to it. The simulation grid is chosen so the FFT lands near the sensor pitch; the residual mismatch is why the example downsamples rather than reads pixels off directly.
checks.name: the_input_spacing_is_close_to_but_not_equal_to_the_camera_pitch

checks.detail: the mask spans 1375.673 rad = 218.95 waves, with an RMS of 184.163 rad. A depth-encoding mask has to be many waves deep; a sub-wave mask could not separate views.
checks.name: the_phase_mask_is_non_trivial_and_many_waves_deep

checks.detail: psf.intensity is (40, 1920, 1920); upstream's psf.shape cell shows the same (40, 1920, 1920) for a 40-element z
checks.name: a_1d_z_gives_a_40_plane_psf_stack

checks.detail: without the mask the brightest pixel stays within 22.0 px of the grid centre at all 40 depths (0 px at most of them): an ordinary 4f system only defocuses, it does not translate the PSF.
checks.name: the_unmasked_psf_peak_never_leaves_the_axis

checks.detail: the unmasked 90%-energy radius mirrored about z = 0 agrees to 0.001% of its mean -- e.g. 155.8 px at z = -100.0 against 155.8 px at z = +100.0. Two emitters equidistant either side of focus are indistinguishable in one 2D image, which is exactly the problem a holoscope solves.
checks.name: the_unmasked_psf_is_symmetric_about_focus_and_so_cannot_encode_the_sign_of_z

checks.detail: the brightest pixel's x offset correlates with z at only r = 0.760072, because the global argmax hops between the six views as z changes (its offset runs [-564.0, -498.0, -502.0, -547.0] ... [547.0, 502.0, 498.0, 561.0] px). Recorded because 'track the argmax' is the obvious way to read the depth code and it does not work; the symmetry-breaking measure below is the one that does.
checks.name: tracking_the_brightest_lobe_is_NOT_a_usable_depth_code

checks.detail: reflecting the unmasked 40-plane stack about z = 0 and differencing gives an RMS of 0.0006% of the stack's own RMS. An ordinary 4f PSF is an even function of defocus, so no 2D measurement can recover the sign of z.
checks.name: the_unmasked_psf_stack_is_symmetric_under_reflection_about_focus

checks.detail: the same reflection test on the engineered stack gives 126.46% against the unmasked 0.0006%, a factor of 225783. The defocused_ramps mask makes the PSF an ODD-containing function of depth, which is precisely what 'optimally encode a 3D volume into a 2D image' requires and what the unmasked system cannot do.
checks.name: the_engineered_psf_stack_breaks_that_symmetry_and_so_encodes_the_sign_of_z

checks.detail: the engineered 90%-energy radius stays in [481.8, 509.7] px against [3.8, 155.8] px unmasked. The six views occupy the field at all depths -- which is the cost of the encoding, and the reason the example needs the crop/taper/downsample chain below.
checks.name: the_engineered_psf_is_spread_over_the_whole_field_at_every_depth

checks.detail: defocused_ramps(..., delta=[1296.0] * 3) -> IndexError: list index out of range. The function indexes delta[ramp_idx] for six fixed ramps, so the six-view geometry is built in and the example's `[1296.0] * 6` is not an arbitrary length.
checks.name: defocused_ramps_requires_exactly_six_delta_entries

checks.detail: seed=972920147 twice gives a bit-identical array (True) and seed=1 gives a different one (True). c14_filaments_phantom reproduces the docs page's UNSEEDED call and records what that gives; this example shows the seeded form, which is what makes a filament phantom usable as a fixture.
checks.name: filaments_3d_is_reproducible_when_given_a_seed

demonstrates: chromatix.utils.defocused_ramps as an engineered pupil phase, objective_point_source over a 1D z, chromatix.utils.center_crop / sigmoid_taper, einops.reduce sum-downsampling, and filaments_3d(seed=...).

metrics.three_ramp_delta_error: IndexError: list index out of range
